video_title: Bitcoin Is the Toll Collector of the AI Economy
gist: Pompliano and Jordy Visser argue AI consumer agents will compress bank multiples (a 'bank apocalypse' as agents arbitrage deposit spreads and stablecoins kill settlement float) and that the best bets are 'toll collectors': agentic compute and crypto financial guardrails. They debate whether value accrues to compute-rich frontier labs (Visser) or to infra/applications as models commoditize (Pompliano), and Visser dismisses Ray Dalio-style bubble talk while predicting crypto's biggest moves come next year via agents.

insights.claim: Jordy Visser expects banks to suffer multiple compression over the next year, analogous to the 'SaaS apocalypse', even if they keep earning money, because AI agents will erode their deposit-spread edge and terminal value.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Bank equities may de-rate despite stable earnings; treat as a multiple story, not an earnings story.
insights.quote: they're going to come under multiple compression over the course of the next year

insights.claim: Banks profit by paying near-zero yield on deposits from lazy consumers and small businesses while investing them in ~4% short-term Treasuries; AI agents that always search for the cheapest/highest-yield option will arbitrage this spread away.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Deposit beta rises structurally as agents manage cash, squeezing net interest margins.
insights.quote: agents are not going to make mistakes. They are going to search for the cheapest way to do thing

insights.claim: Instant settlement via stablecoins and tokenization removes the float that banks, Visa and Mastercard earn from multi-day settlement, adding a second source of pressure on incumbents' margins.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Payment networks and banks reliant on float are exposed as same-day settlement spreads.

insights.claim: Visser frames the SaaS sell-off as a key signal: AI hurt seat-based SaaS stocks despite record earnings, implying exponential AI progress will eventually become a negative for almost every legacy industry.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Expect sector-by-sector de-ratings of legacy incumbents ahead of any earnings damage.

insights.claim: Stripe (about 10,000 employees, ~$160B latest valuation, revenue reportedly up 41% YoY) is positioned as a non-bank competitor already built for crypto and agentic commerce, versus Citi (~$200B market cap with roughly 200,000 people) slowed by bureaucracy and annual bonus/budget cycles.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Nimble payments platforms likely capture the agentic/crypto shift faster than legacy banks.

insights.claim: The winners of agent-driven finance disruption are consumers (lower fees, fair yield) and the 'financial guardrails' (crypto rails); the losers are middlemen.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Position for rail owners over intermediaries.

themes.theme: Big Tech walled gardens vs agents

insights.claim: Amazon blocked Muse and other agents/bots from accessing its site, and Paul Graham argued this is the first time in decades a wedge exists to disrupt Amazon by building an Amazon designed for agents.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Agent-native commerce is a credible attack vector against incumbent marketplaces; Shopify is leaning in.

insights.claim: Visser argues AI agents cut across the previously non-competing business models of the Mag 7, forcing Apple, Amazon and Google to fight for the same consumer-agent TAM and defend turf (e.g., Apple changing iOS to keep agents out), which he reads as a sign their businesses are being disrupted.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Mega-cap moats may erode as they now compete head-on for the agent layer.

insights.claim: Elon Musk said Grok will open its backend to route queries to whichever model is best; Pompliano reads this as a signal that foundation models are commoditizing.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Model routing pressures pricing power of closed labs.

insights.claim: Pompliano's company processing 500 million tokens costs about $5,000 on Claude but is 97% cheaper on its own model and hardware.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Specialized self-hosted models can undercut frontier APIs dramatically on cost for defined workloads.

insights.claim: Pompliano applies crypto's 'fat protocol thesis' to AI: rather than value accruing to model labs, it will accrue mostly to infrastructure and the application layer, making general-purpose models a race to zero.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Favor AI infrastructure and vertical applications over pure model-provider exposure.

insights.claim: Visser disagrees: compute ownership determines model quality, OpenAI, Anthropic and Musk will own most compute (including Vera Rubin), and their best models will be sold to businesses rather than released publicly, so they cannot be distilled or commoditized.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab value persists at the high end; open-source cannot catch up without the compute.
insights.quote: if you have the compute you get the best model

insights.claim: Visser's framework: AI value is about time-to-correct-answer, not just cost; a model reaching an answer in 2 minutes versus a cheaper open model taking 12 minutes can be cheaper in total tokens and time.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Price-per-token comparisons understate the economics of frontier models.
insights.quote: everything in AI is about the time relationship to the probability of getting the right answer

insights.claim: Visser predicts open-source models will handle ~90% of tasks at near-zero cost, while the remaining ~10% of high-end tasks becomes a growing TAM via adoption and Jevons paradox.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Barbell: commoditized bulk plus an expanding premium tier owned by compute-rich labs.

insights.claim: Visser says token demand is still very early: coding agents barely existed a year ago, corporations went through 'token maxing' and are now optimizing spend, and a WSJ piece notes AI spending is becoming nearly impossible for businesses to budget.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Demand-side growth argues against an imminent AI capex bust.

insights.claim: Visser's two investable themes for the next year are agentic compute (AI infrastructure) and financial guardrails (crypto/digital money rails), which he calls the 'toll collectors'; he avoids betting on individual agent apps given global competition.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Own the picks-and-shovels with demand > supply rather than app-layer winners.
insights.quote: I only believe there's two things to focus your attention on the toll collectors

insights.claim: Pompliano believes personal agents like Meta's Muse/Instinct will 'print cash' via transaction-based revenue (taking a vig from merchants, processors and card networks) and better ad targeting from richer data, while Visser counters that the attention economy is going to collapse.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Agent monetization may shift from ads to transaction take-rates, threatening payments economics.

insights.claim: Since ChatGPT, only about 25% of S&P 1500 companies have beaten the index, so returns are highly concentrated; Visser says the highest-probability profits are in compute buildout, plus crypto.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Breadth is poor; concentrate in the compute buildout rather than broad exposure.

insights.claim: Visser predicts next year will see the biggest moves in crypto, driven by AI agents, as traditional finance players increasingly seek him out about tokenization.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Agent-driven TradFi adoption is the catalyst to watch for 2027.
insights.quote: I think next year is going to be the year that we see the biggest moves in crypto because of agents.

insights.claim: Visser calls Bitcoin a bull market because it is above an upward-sloping 200-day moving average, and draws an analogy to Micron, which rose from ~$200 to ~$1,400 after breaking and retesting its 200-day average on an AI theme.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Trend-following signal plus AI narrative suggests patience over trading the chop.

insights.claim: Crypto has risen despite rising rates and falling gold, which Visser sees as evidence of its distancing from both, and acceleration will come when TradFi enters via higher tokenization volumes, tokenized asset size and stablecoin volumes.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Track tokenization and stablecoin volume metrics as leading indicators for crypto upside.

insights.claim: Visser sees research from Citrini, BlackRock and Bloomberg on the crypto–Wall Street/agents intersection as healthy, marking a shift from contrarian to consensus, since you profit only when others later buy the asset.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Broadening institutional narrative is a bullish flow signal.
insights.quote: you are trying to bet where the money is going to go, not where the asset is going to go

insights.claim: Visser expects 10-year yields to be about the same a year from now, lower only if the jobs market weakens noticeably, with AI as the sole growth driver keeping nominal GDP hot and preventing rate cuts.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Higher-for-longer rates coexist with an AI-led run-it-hot economy that favors crypto and compute.

insights.claim: Visser dismisses Ray Dalio's warning that bond yields may prick the AI bubble, noting Dalio's frequent bubble calls and that markets hit new highs despite the pandemic, the fastest Fed hikes, ~10% inflation, SVB, tariffs and a Strait of Hormuz closure this year.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Treat bubble headlines as noise; governments will backstop drawdowns.

insights.claim: Visser, citing page 71 of Situational Awareness, predicts the market chaos and bubble narratives will intensify next year as the speed of AI change accelerates.
insights.speaker: Jordy Visser
insights.so_what: Expect higher volatility and more noise; signal-vs-noise discipline matters more.
